sentences.en: If you're like me, you know this feeling.

And you, you have no idea who you're looking at.

sentences.en: Today on the show, we're talking about faces.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目中，我们来聊聊面孔。

sentences.en: Recognizing faces is a crucial skill.
sentences.zh: 识别人脸是一项至关重要的技能。

sentences.en: It's so crucial that there are regions of the brain devoted to facial recognition.
sentences.zh: 它如此重要，以至于大脑中有专门负责面部识别的区域。

sentences.en: But although your mind is amazing at identifying your boyfriend or your child in a crowd,
sentences.zh: 但尽管你的大脑在人群中识别男友或孩子时表现惊人，

sentences.en: there are important limits to this ability.
sentences.zh: 这种能力也有着重要的局限性。

sentences.en: Some of us, like me, are extremely bad at it.
sentences.zh: 我们中的一些人，比如我，在这方面极其糟糕。
我们中的一些人则表现极佳。

sentences.en: On today's show, we look at some people who are on opposite ends of the spectrum
sentences.zh: 在今天的节目中，我们来看看处于光谱两端的一些人，

sentences.en: and talk about how our ability to recognize faces has broad implications in our lives.
sentences.zh: 并探讨我们识别人脸的能力对我们的生活有着怎样的深远影响。

sentences.en: We'll start with someone whose job requires her to be quick with faces.
sentences.zh: 我们从一个工作要求她能快速认出人脸的人开始。

sentences.en: My name's Alison Young, and I'm a police officer in the Metropolitan Police in London.
sentences.zh: 我叫艾莉森·杨，我是伦敦大都会警察局的一名警官。

sentences.en: She started out several years ago working on response teams in East London.
sentences.zh: 几年前，她开始在伦敦东部的应急小分队工作。

sentences.en: These are the cops who mostly just respond to 911 calls.
sentences.zh: 这些警察主要负责响应911报警电话。

sentences.en: Then, about three and a half years into that job, she and a bunch of her fellow officers
sentences.zh: 然后，在大约入职三年半后，她和一群同事

sentences.en: were invited to take a series of tests at a university.
sentences.zh: 被邀请去一所大学参加一系列测试。

sentences.en: You get given like three or four different faces, and you have to memorize those faces.
sentences.zh: 你会看到大约三到四张不同的面孔，你必须记住这些面孔。

sentences.en: Then a new screen appears with other faces.
sentences.zh: 然后会出现一个新的屏幕，上面有其他面孔。

sentences.en: These ones are obscured in some way, or heavily pixelated.
sentences.zh: 这些面孔经过了某种模糊处理，或者打上了厚厚的马赛克。

sentences.en: One of the faces you saw earlier might now show up wearing a beard.
sentences.zh: 你之前看过的一张面孔现在可能会戴着胡子出现。

sentences.en: So you have to try and work out which one of the faces is the face that you've seen before,

sentences.en: and it's that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 大致就是这种类型的测试。

sentences.en: The test, of course, was measuring how good officers were at recognizing faces.
sentences.zh: 当然，这个测试是在衡量警官们识别人脸的能力有多强。

sentences.en: A while later, Alison received her results.
